claim: Clickjacking overlay attacks are executed structurally via a transparent or near-transparent iframe/element stacked at a higher z-index above a decoy control, or via rapid show/hide of an opaque overlay timed to a click; these are detectable via computed CSS (opacity, z-index, pointer-events), DOM nesting (cross-origin iframes), and geometry (element bounding-box overlap), and modern browsers' Intersection Observer API can programmatically test whether a given element is actually the topmost visible hit-target at its coordinates.

source.title: What is a Clickjacking Attack? [+Examples & Prevention]
source.venue: Vendor security blog (non-academic; used only for the structural/technical mechanism description, not for prevalence claims)

evidence_quote: the hacker hides the original action behind an invisible iframe... positioned above the visible page by setting a higher z-index
